## PKC: Management

Though antituberculin agents are systemically administered, the ocular lesions are appropriately treated with topical steroids. In most instances, patients respond to a potent topical corticosteroid q-i.d. for three to four days, and subsequently tapered according to the clinical response.

Therapy depends on etiol ogy. In individuals who are suspected of having tubercu losis, diagnosis should make use of a purified protein derivative (PPD) skin test, chest radiograph; and sputum cultures if necessary. These individuals should be referred for comanagement to their primary physician or to an infectious disease specialist.

When patients are suspected of underlying staphylococcal disease, both inflammatory and bacterial components can be managed with combination antibioticsteroid such as Zylet. Initial doses should be administered every 2 to 4 hours, depend severity, for the first having ing on
